#2297. Guimaraes will not force Newcastle exit like Isak, says Howe

Eddie Howe is confident Bruno Guimarães will not demand to leave Newcastle United for Arsenal and echo Alexander Isak’s acrimonious departure to Liverpool last summer.

Howe admitted he could not guarantee that Guimarães will still be at the club in September but gave a strong defence of his captain’s character and insisted the Brazil international will return for pre-season training next week as planned.

Given the huge gap between Newcastle’s valuation of Guimarães and what Arsenal have indicated they would be willing to pay for the 28-year-old, there is a belief on Tyneside that the only way the captain would join the London club is if he behaved as badly as Isak did 12 months ago.

Newcastle value Guimarães at £100m, while Arsenal, through intermediaries, have only indicated they would be willing to pay about £60m including bonuses.

Isak did not travel on the club’s pre-season tour to Asia and then went on strike, refusing to train or play, until Newcastle agreed to sell him to Liverpool for a British record £128m on deadline day.

Asked if he feared a repeat of that with Guimarães this time around, Howe replied: “I’ve spoken to him as I would do with Bruno normally. He is a fantastic person and we have had some really good conversations both before, during and after the World Cup. What we speak about obviously has to remain private but he is a great player and a great person.

“Look, I don’t know what is going to happen with Bruno. That is up to other people to speculate about but also other people to have conversations about which I’m not a part of. I don’t think it is fair to compare situations and what happened previously. You’ve got to look at this in its own right.

“Bruno is captain of our football club. He has been an unbelievable player and person all the time we have worked together. I speak on behalf of everyone at the football club when I say we absolutely love him and of course everyone wants him to stay.

“The plan is for him to come back on July 31, he gets an extended break because of the World Cup and is currently enjoying a holiday with his family... There is nothing to say that Bruno won’t be back training with us.”

"We've had some really good conversations" 🗣️Eddie Howe speaks on Newcastle's transfer window so far and speculation around Bruno Guimarães ⚫️⚪️ pic.twitter.com/zB1W31Fne0

Arsenal’s interest in Guimarães is well known but there has been little progress since they began their pursuit more than a month ago.

Whether Arsenal can come up with an offer that tempts Newcastle into negotiations remains to be seen but it is thought the Premier League champions will try to harden up their interest before Guimarães returns for pre-season training.

Newcastle United were held to a 1-1 draw by Gateshead in their second pre-season friendly of the summer. A 79th-minute own-goal saved the Premier League club’s blushes but what did we learn from the match?

Steur did not grab many headlines when he arrived from Ajax for £20m earlier this month because of Sandro Tonali’s move to Tottenham Hotspur. But those familiar with Dutch football would have been excited that Newcastle had signed him.

The 18-year-old has impressed with his performances in training and gave a glimpse of his significant potential in his first public display. He is young and sources have told Telegraph Sport that he must develop physically before he is ready to play every week in the Premier League – but you can already see he has a very high ceiling.

As you would expect from a player described as Ajax’s best midfield prospect for a generation, he is assured on the ball. He is also a progressive passer, always looking to break the lines to get his team moving forward. Eddie Howe will love him.

Whisper it, but there were shades of Bruno Guimarães in his style of play, in the way he took the ball under pressure, in tight spaces, and played on the turn. Patience will be needed but the signs are really encouraging.

Guimarães’s future is all supporters have wanted to speak about for weeks. I was at a wedding on Friday and it felt like everyone asked me about it at some point – including the bride and groom immediately after completing their first dance.

It has already become a summer-long transfer saga that has not progressed since Arsenal’s interest was revealed last month. Telegraph Sport has repeatedly checked whether there have been any fresh developments over the past week and the answer from senior Newcastle sources has remained consistent: there are no talks ongoing and nothing has accelerated, despite claims Arsenal were preparing an official £70m bid.

However, Newcastle need clarity from their captain. He is due back for pre-season next week and is expected to fly to Spain for their training camp on July 31. He has intimated he would like to move to Arsenal but unless Newcastle receive a bid that matches their asking price, he and his representatives have been told he will not be allowed to leave.

Schär has been a brilliant player for Newcastle, but at the age of 34 and coming off the back of a serious ankle injury, he looked understandably rusty against Gateshead.

This will be the former Switzerland international’s ninth season at St James’ Park and he was at fault for giving away a soft free-kick that led to Gateshead scoring first.

Schar accepted a contract extension earlier this summer on reduced terms and although Howe values his quality and experience, he is going to be a back-up centre-back this season.

Neave, 19, started the game as Newcastle’s centre-forward as Will Osula was missing and Nick Woltemade and Yoane Wissa were given additional time off after playing in the World Cup for Germany and DR Congo respectively.

But those players will return to training next week and, although Neave forced a good save in the first half, he is not ready to start in the Premier League. There is little point keeping him around as a fourth-choice striker when he needs to be playing regularly at this stage of his career.

A loan move is on the cards and he could be a really smart signing for a Championship club or a team competing at the top of League One. The most important thing is that he gets regular senior games rather than hangs around at Newcastle on the fringes of the first-team squad.

Eddie Howe has said "he does not know" what will happen with Bruno but pretty strong defence of his character and denied similarities with Isak. Said they have spoken regularly throughout the summer and he will be back for pre season training on July 31st #nufc

Eddie Howe’s side will head down to Ashton Gate before jetting off to La Manga for a training camp on July 31, which will feature many of those who played in the World Cup, including Bruno Guimarães who has been linked with a move to Arsenal.

In Spain, Newcastle will face Valencia at the Mestalla, before returning to the UK to play Everton at Murrayfield. They will then host Bayer Leverkusen and Strasbourg at St James’ Park for their final tune-up matches before the Premier League season starts.

This is their pre-season schedule in full:

The referee brings this contest to a close and it finishes a goal apiece at Gateshead International Stadium. Not the result Howe was hoping for, but he can at least find some comfort in a positive showing from new signing Steur in the heart of midfield.

Newcastle ended up with 76 per cent of the ball and created three ‘big chances’ but lacked the cutting edge in the final third to make that dominance tell. Credit must go to Gateshead who defended resolutely and took their best chance of the match.

Important pre-season minutes 👊 pic.twitter.com/FpzYVdbc0C

The hosts have near enough seven bodies in their back line and Newcastle are struggling to find a way through.

Bone picks Pivas’ pocket on the edge of the box but the Serbian defender does well to recover and Jaouen gets a rare touch on the ball as he clears his lines.

Newcastle have five minutes, plus added time, to grab a go-ahead goal. Plenty of industry on show from the youngsters who have come on, but the play has largely been restricted to a midfield slug-fest in the last minutes.

Triple substitution from Howe. Hall, Ramsey and Willock make way for Salia, Munda and Charlton.

Gateshead 1 Newcastle 1 (OG) Hall’s cross from the left in turned by Williams. Newcastle had been turning the screw as Gateshead dropped deeper and deeper.

The stadium announcer tells us that there are 7,195 people at this afternoon’s match.

Sanusi and Park replace Murphy and Barnes.

There is the first yellow card of the match. Home lands an overzealous challenge on Willock in the centre of the pitch and receives a booking for his troubles.

Ferreira is then played into the left channel and unleashes a shot which is turned behind for a corner by Desbois, who has been awesome this afternoon.

Jaouen, Miley and Ferreira replace Pope, Shahar and Neave.

Gateshead are sitting deeper meaning that their penalty area is often getting quite congested.

There are opportunities for the hosts to counter, though, and Boatswain has the chance to play in Telford but severely overhits the through-ball.

A note on Steur... He’s completed 65 of his 68 attempted passes so far. That’s 96 per cent. Impressive stuff.

Hall falls on to the ball under pressure on the byline. The referee awards a free-kick to Gateshead and Hall protests his case. Just not happening for the left-back, who has been given the licence to get forward.

Schar makes way for Pivas at the hour mark. Gateshead respond with a double change.

Hall is brought down in the Gateshead box by Ferguson as he tears towards the byline. He wants a penalty but the referee awards a corner – there is a momentary confrontation between the two players but they settle their differences quickly.

Murphy switches wings to create an overload with Barnes down the left and flashes a cross into the box which is dealt with by Gateshead. Newcastle need more invention like that if they are to break down this stubborn Gateshead side.

Chance for Newcastle! Steur releases Barnes into the left channel and he plays the ball across goal but just in front of Neave who had the freedom of Tyneside at the back post. Desbois is called into action moments later, punching the ball clear after some pinball in the box.

Steur shifts the ball on to his left foot and has a go from 25 yards out, firing the ball high and wide. Good intent, though.

Ramsey is dropping in to receive the ball to feet. His average position in the first half was significantly more withdrawn than Willock’s, and Howe will surely look to get him further up the pitch to affect play in the final third in the second period.

An immediate chance for the hosts’ front man Boatswain at the start of the second half. The ball just gets away from him.

Newcastle have work to do and, unlike last weekend against Darlington, Howe sticks with the same XI at the start of the second period. Gateshead also unchanged.

A moment of silence impeccably observed in memory of King Kev 🖤🤍 pic.twitter.com/TmeQ5A64jN

Newcastle go into the break a goal down. There have been chances for the visitors, who dominated the ball in that first period. Expect changes at the interval.

How has Barnes missed that?! A lovely ball in from the right comes through a thicket of limbs and lands at the winger’s feet only a couple of yards out from goal. He can’t make a meaningful contact on the ball and the chance passes him by.

Gateshead’s goal came against the run of play and was there first shot on target. It’s not great from Fabian Schar, who conceded the free kick competing for a long ball down the middle and Nick Pope was a little slow off his line to smother the shot too.

Gateshead 1 Newcastle 0 (Supyk) Gateshead win a free-kick 25 yards out, just to the right of the D. Chadwick’s initial effort ricochets through the wall and new signing Supyk is first on to the scene to prod the ball beyond Pope. A calamity at the back for Howe’s side!

Our Kiwi just can't stop scoring! 🇳🇿😄 https://t.co/Z0cjcEadvG pic.twitter.com/6Kca67vFom

Neave comes close to opening the scoring, firing an effort across the face of goal that goes behind for a corner.

Hall then gets a shot away from the edge of the box, but cannot keep his half-volley down and the ball sails over the bar.

Newcastle look most dangerous when Schar steps up and punches in those line-breaking passes. Gateshead defending resolutely, though, keeping things compact across the backline.

Murphy earns his side a free-kick down the right. He delivers the ball himself, with the box loaded with Schar and Murphy, and the former steals in to the near post but cannot quite stoop down low enough to get a meaningful contact on the ball. Desbois gathers without fuss.

Newcastle have won a glut of corners down their left, all of which have been taken short. The latest is played out to Steur who rains in a cross which is claimed by the goalkeeper.

Sean Steur looks like a player... some really nice touches from the young Dutchman. He is always looking to make a progressive pass and has been a real bright spark. Newcastle have dominated the game. As you would expect against opposition four divisions below them

Another tidy involvement from Steur, who disguises a pass to Ramsey on the edge of the box. The ball is worked into the path of Murphy and deflects out for a corner. The former Ajax midfielder is growing in confidence.

Hall puts in another ball from the left, this time to the back post, where the ball is headed away by Ferguson.

New signing Steur is starting to creep forward, carrying the ball nicely and picking it back up in the right channel. He stands a cross up to the near post but Murphy’s header is dealt with by Desbois.

Hall works a yard of space in a dangerous area down the left moments later, but the ball ricochets back off him and out for goal-kick.

Hall punches in a lovely ball down the line for Barnes to run on to, but the move is snuffed out by Robinson.

It does seem strange that this game has not sold out. There are thought to be about 7,000 fans inside the stadium, which once had a capacity of more than 11,000 when it was one of the country’s premier athletics venues. They even used to have Diamond League events here not so long ago.

But the capacity has been steadily reduced for safety reasons and it is rarely used for anything other than local athletic events and Gateshead FC games.

There were officially only 50 tickets left for sale a few minutes before kick-off, but there are lots of empty seats.

Chadwick lofts a tidy cross in from the left, but Boatswain’s header drifts wide of the mark. The chance came off a decent spell of possession from Cattermole’s side, the most fluent they have been in this match so far.

Ramsey regains possession high up the pitch and releases Barnes who plays in Murphy, but the Newcastle forward mistimes his run and the linesman’s flag goes up. A promising counter.

Ramsey is brought down on the edge of the box as he tries to break free and the referee awards a free-kick. There are a few contenders to take it (Schar, Barnes, Hall) but in the end it is Barnes who gets a shot away, but his curled effort flies just wide of the mark.

Another weighted ball over the top from Schar puts Anifowose under pressure in the left channel but his ball across the face of goal is cleared to safety by a team-mate.

Newcastle circulating the ball in front of Gateshead’s first line of pressure. The hosts regain possession but struggle to find a way through Newcastle’s midfield.

Schar getting a few early touches as he makes his return from injury. He plays a long, raking diagonal out to Barnes who cannot quite get past his man.

Neave tests Desbois with a well-struck effort off the next phase of play.

The officials and both sets of players line up behind a banner with the message ‘Rest in peace, Kevin Keegan’. Newcastle are in their new navy-blue away shirt, with Gateshead in their home white-and-black kit. A minute’s silence is then observed immaculately.

The tributes left in honour of Kevin Keegan outside St James’ Park is a sight to behold, with flowers, shirts and scarves covering the ground and steps in the south-west corner. It is a very moving thing to behold as people come to pay their respects to the Newcastle legend.

There will also be a minute’s silence before today’s game against Gateshead.

Some time tidy centre-forward play from Levi Amantchi in last week’s 3-3 draw. The target man has since been loaned to Kidderminster Harriers...

A post shared by Gateshead FC (@gfc_official)

Incomings Bazoumana Touré ⇠ Hoffenheim, £43mAladji Bamba ⇠ Monaco, £30mSean Steur ⇠ Ajax, £20mEwen Jaouen ⇠ Stade Reims, £18m

OutgoingsSandro Tonali ⇢ Tottenham Hotspur, £92.5mAnthony Gordon ⇢ Barcelona, £68mKieran Trippier ⇢ Wolverhampton Wanderers, FreeMatt Targett ⇢ Hull City, FreeEmil Krafth, FreeJohn Ruddy, Free

It has been a difficult and, at times, acrimonious 12 months for Eddie Howe, who must have wondered whether the job was still worth the hassle given the criticism and online vitriol he received at times last season.

Few would have blamed him if he had quit, but Howe has always been fully committed and always knew there would be a period like this to come through.

He has been in the job almost five years and last season was the first time he had been vilified by a section of the fanbase. It left its mark. The boos that followed defeats at St James’ Park hurt and he worried the unity that had powered the team’s success had fractured irreparably.

The apparent collective shrug that greeted another run to the Carabao Cup semi-final, while guiding the team into the knockout rounds of the Champions League for the first time was a source of bewilderment and frustration.

Howe has not complained or moaned. Although he wobbled towards the end of last season and there were some calling for him to be sacked, he was supported and encouraged by those above him. That loyalty mattered.

The problem is, negativity lingers in the fanbase. Even a picture of Howe at pre-season training, posted on social media by the club, led to abusive comments questioning his ability and character. Some of it was toxic. It was rightly called out by other supporters.

Goals from Elliot Anderson (wonder what happened to him?!), Allan Saint-Maximin and Jay Turner-Cooke helped Newcastle overturn a 2-0 half-time deficit when they last visited Gateshead International Stadium in 2023.

Speaking through Gateshead’s club media, Cattermole said of facing Newcastle: “It’s obviously a different test. We have to respect the opposition, they’re a high-quality team and it might not be what we’re getting in our league but we’ll still try to implement what we believe we want to be in and out of possession. It’ll be a great physical challenge for us.

He added: “They [my players] have all shown up great. What a game for them. What a game for them to go and test yourself against some big names and fantastic coaching staff, for us all it’s a great challenge for us. We hope we give them a good test, we hope we give them the challenge they want as well. I played in many of these games as a player as well. We expect it to be competitive.”

💬 "What a game for [the players] to go & play."Lee Cattermole talks tomorrow's game against @NUFC at the GIS ⤵️📺👉 https://t.co/DGuJRosJ2K pic.twitter.com/rccs5FzhG6

A classic first-game-of-pre-season vibe to Newcastle’s team sheet as established stars rub shoulders with youngsters from the academy.

Only one of their four summer signings, former Ajax midfielder Sean Steur, starts the game and there will be a lot of interest in the 18-year-old. The youngster has impressed in training over the last couple of weeks but it is thought he has a lot of work to do physically to be ready for the Premier League.

Full-back Leo Shahar was in and around the first team last season as was striker Sean Neave. Alex Murphy, who started one game in the Champions League last season is expected to go out on loan before the window shuts, but starts alongside Fabian Schar in the centre of defence.

Worryingly there is no sign of Sven Botman and Will Osula who both played in the behind-closed-doors friendly against Darlington last weekend.

Joelinton, Tino Livramento and Lewis Miley are still being eased back into things after injuries at the end of last season.

Another new signing, goalkeeper Ewen Jaouen, is on the bench and will play the second half against their National League neighbours.

Gateshead lost manager Rob Elliot to Carlisle at the end of last season and are now managed by former Sunderland and Middlesbrough midfielder Lee Cattermole.

Arrivals in Gateshead 👋 pic.twitter.com/9hTtruxGEo

Ready for our return to the GIS! 🤍🔢 pic.twitter.com/lg1TfjyD6q

Fabian Schär returns from an ankle injury that has sidelined him since January, but only one of Newcastle’s four summer signings (Sean Steur) starts.

Welcome to live coverage of Newcastle United’s pre-season friendly against North-East neighbours Gateshead. Eddie Howe’s side make the three-mile journey south of the River Tyne having beaten Darlington 3-0 in their first outing of the summer last weekend. The Magpies’ National League opponents this afternoon, helmed by former Sunderland captain Lee Cattermole, have already played three times in pre-season, thrashing Blyth 6-0 and drawing against Heaton Stannington and Hebburn Town. The Heed threatened a shock win in their last meeting with Newcastle three summers’ ago, leading 2-0 at the interval before conceding three second-half goals.

This contest at Gateshead International Stadium will be Newcastle’s first match since the death of Kevin Keegan and the club have confirmed that a minute of silence will be observed before kick-off. Newcastle’s men’s, women’s and academy teams will wear black armbands for all pre-season matches this summer.

Newcastle United's men's, women's and Under-21s teams will wear black armbands across all pre-season matches this summer as the club honours the life of Kevin Keegan.Full details ⤵️

Newcastle will welcome Liverpool, with whom Keegan enjoyed success in the 1970s, to St James’ Park for their Premier League opener, and the two sides are in talks over a suitable pre-match tribute. Flowers, messages and mementos have been laid outside Newcastle’s ground since Keegan’s death on Monday, including a heartfelt message penned by fellow club legend Alan Shearer, which read: “I hope you realised how much you meant, to me, to this club, to everyone. Thank you does not seem enough. Rest In Peace Boss. Alan Shearer.”

With regards to the football, there is an acceptance among Newcastle supporters that, having finished 12th in the Premier League last season and lost Anthony Gordon, Kieran Trippier and Sandro Tonali, this is a summer of transition. The uncertainty surrounding the future of £100m-rated club captain Bruno Guimarães, who is on the radar of Arsenal, will be a concern; Newcastle will be keen to avoid a repeat of the furore that circled Alexander Isak’s departure last summer. Guimarães will join the team next week following his World Cup exploits with Brazil and is expected to take part in Newcastle’s La Manga training camp, which starts on July 31.

Summer signings Sean Steur and Ewen Jaouen were each handed 45 minutes in the behind-closed-doors victory over Darlington, during which Howe used different XIs for the two halves. Bazoumana Touré – the £50m winger acquired from Hoffenheim – is expected to feature today having returned from his post-World Cup holiday. Yesterday Newcastle announced the arrival of midfielder Aladji Bamba, the France youth international, from Monaco and he was immediately integrated into team training. There is every possibility that he will feature this afternoon. Gateshead this week announced two signings of their own, as Luke Supyk, the New Zealand Under-20 forward, agreed a two-year deal having scored three goals in pre-season as a trialist. Defender Jack Robinson also joined the club.

#2296. Napoli Lazio, Gattuso potrebbe fare a meno di Nuno Tavares: Zaccagni già è out

La Lazio potrebbe presentarsi al Maradona con un’altra assenza pesante. Dopo Zaccagni, infatti, anche Nuno Tavares rischia di saltare la trasferta contro il Napoli, in programma domenica alle 12:30. Come riferito da Il Messaggero, il laterale portoghese ha accusato un affaticamento al flessore che gli ha impedito di prendere parte all’allenamento di ieri. Le sue condizioni saranno valutate attentamente nelle prossime ore, ma al momento la presenza a Napoli resta in forte dubbio. Per Gattuso si tratterebbe di una doppia defezione significativa, considerando anche l’indisponibilita’ di Zaccagni. Due possibili assenze che potrebbero condizionare le scelte del tecnico in vista di una gara particolarmente delicata. Situazione complicata anche sul fronte Napoli. Dopo la pesante sconfitta contro il Porto, Massimiliano Allegri deve preparare una sfida decisiva senza recuperare nuovi giocatori. Le scelte del tecnico toscano restano quindi praticamente obbligate, proprio come accaduto nella trasferta europea in Portogallo.

#2294. Rambaudi avvisa la Lazio: “Non devi andare a Napoli e pensare di gestire la partita”

Le analisi e i consigli di Roberto Rambaudi in vista del big match di Serie A fra Lazio e Napoli

In vista della sfida contro il Napoli, l'ex giocatore della Lazio Roberto Rambaudi ha analizzato a Radiosei la pesante assenza di Mattia Zaccagni e l'approccio tattico e mentale con cui la squadra capitolina dovrà affrontare il match al Maradona.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM

Zaccagni è quello che salta l'uomo, fa assist, crea superiorità; sarà un test per chi prende il suo posto. Ad ogni modo, nonostante il Napoli sia in difficoltà, la vittoria non è mai scontata. Sono forti ma non sono nella condizione mentale ottimale. Immagino la squadra verrà contestata; alcuni giocatori, i più importanti e rappresentativi, proveranno a dare una scossa, in casa, prima della sosta. Non devi andare a Napoli e pensare di gestire la partita, credo che molto si deciderà nei primi 20-25', se li fai galvanizzare o se li metti subito in difficoltà, creando dall'inizio.

Se Tavares e Pedraza stanno bene, potrebbe essere un'opzione vedere loro due dal 1' a sinistra. Credo sia una scelta che Gattuso farà in base a come vede i calciatori durante la settimana. Magari anche Cancellieri a sinistra può essere una soluzione, io Isaksen da destra non lo toglierei.

#2293. Italiano si mangia le mani, remuntada Bournemouth: Europa League, risultati e classifica

Al tramonto del quarto turno di League Phase di Europa League, i risultati maturati sui campi continentali offrono verdetti e colpi di scena. L'Anderlecht supera agilmente e con un gol per tempo il Salisburgo, mentre il Crystal Palace agguanta un insperato pareggio per 1-1 grazie al guizzo dell'ex Lazio Kamada al 91'.

Protagonista di una rimonta straordinaria è il Bournemouth, autore di un secondo tempo eccezionale con cui ribalta lo Sparta Praga (da 0-1 a 3-1) e centra una vittoria esterna pesantissima, al pari del NEC Nijmegen ai danni dell'Omonia. Stesso punteggio di 1-1 per il Lione che, orfano di Paulo Fonseca e alla prima uscita con Maciel in panchina, impatta a San Sebastian contro la Real Sociedad grazie alla firma di Tolisso, mentre la vittoria di misura strappata dal Levski lascia i polacchi dello Jagiellonia fuori dalla zona playoff e appena dietro il Milan di Ruben Amorim.

Nelle altre sfide della serata, oltre all'affermazione esterna della Juventus, il Benfica cala il tris contro il Lech blindando la vetta della classifica, il Celta Vigo cade a sorpresa al cospetto dei belgi dell'Union SG. Serata amara anche per il Besiktas di Vincenzo Italiano, sconfitto per mano del Celtic a Glasgow in un momento di flessione europea caratterizzato da un pari e un ko nelle ultime due uscite.

Ko rocambolesco per l'Ararat Armenia, che si butta via perdendo 3-2 in parità numerica contro i portoghesi del Torreense. Sorride invece l'OFI Creta con tre punti pesanti sull'Hapoel Beer Sheva, il Marsiglia espugna con autorità il campo di Leverkusen e il Sunderland delude le attese uscendo sconfitto per 2-0 dal duello casalingo con la Dinamo Zagabria.

#2292. Napoli, Allegri in bilico: dalla Francia avanza l’ipotesi Sergio Conceicao

Sergio Conceicao è un serio candidato per la panchina del Napoli, qualora Massimiliano Allegri dovesse lasciare l’incarico. A scriverlo su X è il giornalista di Footmercato Santi Aouna, che aggiunge: “L’allenatore portoghese è tenuto in grande considerazione dal presidente De Laurentiis. Conceicao è andato molto vicino a diventare l’allenatore del Napoli sia nel 2021 che nel 2023, ma in quelle occasioni l’FC Porto aveva preteso il pagamento dell’intera clausola rescissoria. Di recente, il tecnico ha rifiutato il Fenerbahce poichè preferisce un ruolo in uno dei cinque principali campionati europei”.

#2291. Chelsea in 10-goal thriller as ‘Alonso ball’ brings risk and reward

Chelsea’s first match under the management of Xabi Alonso was a 10-goal thriller in Australia, as the Premier League side eventually showed their class in a 6-4 win over Western Sydney Wanderers.

Star striker João Pedro, who was controversially left out of Brazil’s World Cup squad, scored a nine-minute hat-trick after coming off the bench with half an hour of the friendly remaining.

Alonso had selected a youthful team for the first hour before bringing nine senior players, including João Pedro, into the side in the second half. According to Transfermarkt, Chelsea’s squad is valued at over £1.3bn while their opponents a more modest £5.86m.

Teenage signing Dastan Satpayev, midfielder Dario Essugo and winger Jamie Gittens also found the net for Chelsea, who were defensively vulnerable for long spells for the game.

Here are five things Telegraph Sport learned from Alonso’s first match.

João Pedro scored 13 goals in the second half of last season and his impressive performances resulted in the 24-year-old being named Chelsea’s player of the campaign. It was something of a surprise, then, when he was left out of Carlo Ancelotti’s Brazil squad this summer.

The good news for Chelsea is that João Pedro’s absence from the World Cup has given him plenty of time to recover ahead of the new campaign, and he looked thrillingly sharp in his second-half performance against Western Sydney Wanderers. The difference in class between João Pedro and Liam Delap, the man he replaced, was clear for all to see.

Two of the Brazilian’s three goals were classy, composed finishes — and he also created a goal for Gittens after surging past three defenders on the left wing. João Pedro looks like he means business.

As expected, Alonso tasked his players with deploying a possession-based strategy in which the ball is worked from back to front between the lines. At times, Alonso’s vision was executed in style: Chelsea’s two goals in the first half were both the consequence of slick passing moves.

There were plenty of other occasions, though, when Chelsea were sloppy in their passing and defensively exposed when they lost the ball. The best example of this was in the second half, when Estêvão’s error allowed Western Sydney Wanderers to score their fourth goal of the game.

Admittedly, Chelsea’s attempts to play passing football were not helped by the poor quality of the pitch in Sydney. A recent rugby game had created a bobbly, unpredictable surface which caused no end of problems for Chelsea’s midfield players. That may sound like an excuse for their sloppiness, but it is probably a fair one.

Chelsea started the game with two Reggies in their midfield. Reggie Walsh is a 17-year-old technician who last year became the club’s third-youngest player, and was loved by former head coach Enzo Maresca. He played as the No 10.

Reggie Watson, meanwhile, is the son of former Premier League midfielder Ben and is one of the most exciting talents in English football. A composed central midfielder, Watson is a regular for England’s youth teams and is the youngest player on Chelsea’s pre-season tour.

Both players showed glimpses of their talent in this match in Sydney. Watson was trusted with set-piece duties and produced some excellent deliveries, while also playing some lovely passes through the lines. Watson was the only Chelsea player to feature for the full 90 minutes, which spoke volumes of the quality of his performance.

Walsh was less involved but caught the eye in a couple of moments, not least when playing a delicate one-two with Essugo in advance of the midfielder’s first-half strike.

Satpayev is technically not a Chelsea player yet, as his deal officially commences when he turns 18 in August. His former club, Kairat, gave special dispensation to allow the teenager to join Chelsea’s pre-season tour ahead of the completion of his £3m transfer, which means he is officially in Australia as a “triallist”.

Satpayev is a player of obvious talent and has already played nine games for Kazakhstan. Before this move to Chelsea, he scored 21 goals in 41 games in the Kazakhstan Premier League.

The first sighting of Satpayev was an exciting one for Chelsea supporters, who saw the new man’s running speed and shooting power as he scored the opening goal of the game. Running in behind the Western Sydney Wanderers defence, Satpayev surged clear of the opposition and launched a scorching shot into the roof of the net.

Gittens endured a hugely disappointing first campaign at Chelsea last season, following his £52m move from Borussia Dortmund. Injury issues did not help his cause but he struggled to make much of an impact when he was fully fit, scoring just one goal in 27 appearances in all competitions.

Gittens is therefore a man with it all to prove at Stamford Bridge this season, and he has started the new campaign in promising form. His goal here came after two strikes in two behind-closed-doors friendly games before Chelsea left for Australia. Gittens was a constant threat after coming onto the pitch in the 63rd minute, showing his pace on the wing and his ability to go down the touchline or cut inside. His challenge now is to replicate this level of performance against better opposition.

A late revival ensures Chelsea win their first pre-season friendly under Xabi Alonso. There was a step up in class once Palmer, Pedro, Gittens, Estevao and Palestra were introduced, and the Australian side could not contain them. No injuries on a dogy pitching probably the biggest victory for the new manager.

Just the three minutes of added time to play.

Three goals in nine minutes for the Brazilian. Excellent corner delivery from Estevao, Fofana’s header blocked but then Joao Pedro turns home from close range. Baffling decision by Brazil not to take him to the World Cup.

Chelsea flooding forward again, and they have a corner in the last minute of normal time.

Chelsea now lead 5-4, Cole Palmer picking out Joao Pedro with the through ball but Western Sydney Wanderers were far too open. Joao Pedro shows his composure, sitting the defender down and rolling the ball into the bottom corner.

Estevao shows he has not lost his burst of speed after that serious hamstring injury but his shot flies straight into the side netting. Joao Pedro then delights the crowd with another piece of skill.

Jamie Gittens is having a good pre-season, having scored in two behind-closed-doors friendlies before this game in Australia. He has looked sharp since coming off the bench and has been involved in two of Chelsea’s goals.

Gittens had a disappointing first season at Chelsea following his £52m move from Dortmund last summer and is clearly keen to impress Alonso.

Robert Sanchez picks out Gittens with a raking pass, but his shot is blocked. The same is true for Joao Pedro’s follow up attempt. Gittens has impressed since coming on.

Poor defensive header back into a dangerous area from Gittens’s cross, but it is a crisp touch and finish from Joao Pedro, picking out the bottom corner. Chelsea level at 4-4. The move started with a quick free-kick, from Palmer, which he won.

Western Sydney Wanderers score their fourth goal of the game. Chelsea make another error when playing out from the back, it was Estevao who sold Reggie Watson short. One pass and one shot later, Awan Lual finishes beyond Sanchez.

Mazy run inside from Estevao off the right flank, but there was not quite enough power in his shot to beat the goalkeeper.

Joao Pedro is very good at taking the ball in and making it stick. Palestra looks very progressive from right-back, looks full of running and attacking intent.

Some of Western Sydney Wanderers’s corner routines have been quite nifty, Chelsea opened up from a short one again. Palmer with a velvety touch in midield and pass forward towards Palestra who was breaking forward.

Gittens scores, and the introduction of the senior players has made a difference already. Levi Colwill started the move with a longer pass forward, before Joao Pedro skips through challenges to tee up Gittens.

Nine changes made by Alonso: Palmer, Estevao, Palestra, Gittens, Sanchez, Colwill, Anselmino, Joao Pedro and Fofana are the players who have come on.

The Australian side now lead. Emenalo’s clearance deflects off a Western Sydney Wanderers player, and falls kindly to Scicluna, who drills his show beyond Sharman-Lowe into the bottom corner. He come the Chelsea changes.

Western Sydney Wanderers playing some good football in the last few minutes, Saptaev outmuscled in midfield and a shot comes in from the edge of the area. Sharman-Lowe saves, then Tosin clears after a short corner routine.

This young Chelsea side, which is still dealing with jet lag, looks a little tired now. They have not been under huge pressure but they can hardly complain about falling 3-2 behind. Here come all the big names, as Alonso makes huge changes for the last 30 minutes.

Chelsea enjoying a spell of comfortable possession, the tempo of the game has dropped. Good play again, from Reggie Watson, finding Emenalo on the overlap but he slices his shot high and wide when there was time to take aim.

Chelsea remain committed to passing out from the back, but the uneven pitch is making that difficult. Sharman-Lowe passes the ball straight out for a throw-in. Good defending from Acheampong to deal with a teasing cross.

Chelsea win a free-kick in a shooting position, and Reggie Watson takes it with his right foot. He goes goalkeeper’s side but, it shot curls just wide of the post.

Western Sydney Wanderers kick off in the second half.

Kellyman on for Essugo in midfield, and Nicoll-Jazuli replaces Kavuma-McQueen.

Some eye-catching football from Chelsea going forward, but some loose defending too. Suspect it is not long before we see Palmer, Estevao, Colwill and Joao Pedro. Walsh and Watson have done well in midfield for Chelsea.

Half-time! 🕰️Watch the second half LIVE on CFC+ 📺

Another really bad miss from Tosin. Free header from a corner, could see it all the way, but he skewed the ball wide from a just a couple of yards out. Chelsea should be in front.

Subuloye wins a back post header from the Chelsea corner, but the “home” team clear. More goals in this game, surely. Saptaev wins Chelsea a corner with another burst forward.

This is a great team goal. Essugo started the move, finding Saptaev down the left. Essugo moves the ball on two Walsh, who gives it him back with a slick one-two and Essugo rolls the ball into the bottom corner.

That’s the second impressive team goal that Chelsea have scored in this first half. Essugo to Walsh, Walsh to Essugo, Essugo finds the corner. Walsh, 17, has produced some nice touches in the No 10 position. Last year he became the third-youngest player in Chelsea’s history and you can see he is a supremely talented teenager.

Chelsea in trouble defensively again, passing their way into trouble on the edge of their defensive third. I’m sure there will be a raft of half-time changes, but that was probably the plan all along.

Chelsea have been alarmingly open and easy to play through. The collective structure and individual defending were both poor in advance of that second Western Sydney Wanderers goal. I expect they’ll tighten up when the more experienced players come into the game.

Hammond is the goalscorer, and it is a finish of genuine quality. Silky touch to flick the ball inside Josh Acheampong, and fire low into the bottom corner. Soft Chelsea defending, though.

Smooth combination play from Walsh and Watson, the two Reggies in Chelsea’s midfield, before Saptaev shoots over the bar form the edge of the box. A shame for marketing people and headline writers that one of Walsh or Watson are not called Ronnie.

Reggie Watson with a foul in midfield. Fair to say Chelsea’s youthful team are on the back foot now, but there was nice turn in midfield from Essugo after more passing out from the back. Clear that is an emphasis for Alonso.

Sharman-Lowe claims a cross, but Western Sydney Wanderers down their right flank again. I almost anticipated a hydration break at this stage, but it is back to business as usual. Chelsea flagging a touch after a lively start.

Chelsea’s defence looking a touch exposed again, but Borrello curls a shot wide of the post. Emenalo has down well going forward but there was space down his side there.

Two causes for concern for Chelsea in the first 15 minutes here. The first is the pitch in Sydney, which looks terrible. The ball is bobbling all over midfield, making it very difficult for Chelsea’s central players in particular. The second concern will be their defending for that set-piece, as Western Sydney Wanderers had two free headers.

Liam Delap has not been particularly involved, but Reggie Watson almost found him with a cute reverse pass. Watson the plays a progressive pass forward from deep.

Reggie Walsh pushes forward and takes on a shot from long range. Well struck, another save from the goalkeeper. From the resulting corner, taken by Watson, Tosin misses a free header. Good chance, should have hit the target.

Chelsea concede from the corner. Flicked on at the near post and a free header at the back stick for Anthony Pantazopoulos. One for Austin MacPhee, Chelsea’ new set-piece coach, to clip up and show in the team meeting.

Emenalo fouled after more neat football out from the back by Chelsea. Alonso is on his feet on the touchline, barking instructions. Emenalo has showed some silky touches.

Chance for Western Sydney Wanderers though, nut Sharman-Lowe tips Gillion’s shot around the post.

The pitch is very, very bobbly. Excellent strike from Kavuma-McQueen for Chelsea, but Holmes tips the shot around the post.

Was that the first glimpse of “Alonso-ball”? It’s a lovely team goal, worked from back to front with some incisive passing. Terrific, powerful finish by Dastan Satpayev, the 17-year-old Kazakh, who joined from FC Kairat this summer. He already has nine caps for Kazakhstan.

Technically speaking, Satpayev is not officially a Chelsea player yet and is a “triallist” on this tour. He will be formally unveiled when he turns 18 in August.

The 17-year-old summer signing from Kairat Almaty has put Chelsea in front. It was a nice move from their own defensive third, drawing Western Sydney Wanderers on creating a two-on-two against their defence. Satpaev goes through and blasts a shot into the roof of the net. Good through ball from Ryan Kavuma-McQueen.

Chelsea youngsters Walsh and Watson do well in midfield, and they have a free-kick on halfway. Reggie Watson is the son of former Crystal Palace and Wigan Athletic midfielder Ben. A couple of stray kicks from Chelsea’s goalkeeper Teddy Sharman-Lowe. An opening for the hosts, but Hammond’s strike is wayward.

Landon Emenalo is playing at left wing-back, and he is the son of former Chelsea director of football Michael. He has had one burst forward already, and is called into some early defending to concede a throw in.

Chelsea get the game under way. The pitch looks very patchy. Incredible how clubs are willing to play mutli-million pound assets on surfaces like this.

Western Sydney Wanderers in horizontal red and black stripes, Chelsea in the season’s new blue home kit.

Off the bus. 🚎 pic.twitter.com/0sBDuEtzog

A very youthful team from the start, with some big hitters on the bench. Dastan Satpaev, 17, is a £2.1m summer signing from Kairat Almaty.

Chelsea XI: Sharman-Lowe, Acheampong, Tosin, Subuloye, Emenalo, Walsh, Watson, Essugo, Delap, Satpaev, Kavuma-McQueen

Subs: Sanchez, Curd, Palestra, Colwill, Fofana, Anselmino, Diakite, Lavia, Kellyman, Nicoll-Jazuli, Palmer, Gittens, Estevao, Joao Pedro

Chelsea started their pre-season with a 3-0 victory over Bromley in a behind-closed-doors friendly, but this morning we will have our first proper look at Xabi Alonso’s team as they take on Western Sydney Wanderers.

There was some interesting news from Stamford Bridge on Monday when it emerged the club are in talks to sign Danny Welbeck and Jordan Henderson. Coming after the fruitless pursuit of Granit Xhaka, the strategy suggests that Alonso has made cultural improvement a priority in a dressing room that has been accused of lacking discipline and leadership.

As ever, Chelsea have been busy in the transfer market with Morgan Rogers and Marco Palestra their headline signings, and Geovany Quenda joins up with the club from Sporting CP having been signed in March 2025.

Rogers is yet to join up with his new team-mates following his World Cup exertions with England, but fans will be looking forward to seeing how he combines with Cole Palmer.

“In that position, we needed an important player, and I’m sure that there were not many more better options than Morgan,” the 44-year-old manager told reporters. “It means a lot for everyone.”

Tasked with reviving Chelsea after a turbulent, trophyless season in which the west London club finished 10th ⁠in the Premier League, Alonso believes Rogers can combine effectively with Palmer.

“I have a plan. I have an idea. I can see them linking really well,” Alonso said of ​Rogers and Palmer, who are close ‌friends and England teammates.

“You need to have a good mix, good stability players, and players that can play with more freedom.

“And if we get that ‌balance right, ​and we get ⁠those special players in the right positions, with good control, I think that we will be more ⁠competitive with the ball ​and against the ball.”

#2290. Calabria trascina il Panathinaikos, forza bruta Ajax: Conference League, risultati e classifica

Si chiude anche il terzo turno di League Phase di Conference League, una serata ricca di gol e sorprese. L'Ajax ha travolto i danesi del Midtjylland con un netto 6-1, perentorio successo in cui è arrivata anche la marcatura dell'ex Inter Davy Klaassen. L'impresa del giorno giunge però da Gibilterra, dove il Lincoln ha ribaltato ogni pronostico sconfiggendo l'Hajduk Spalato, mentre gli svedesi del Mjallby si sono imposti per 2-0 sui bosniaci del Borac Banja Luka e appena fuori dalla top-8.

Finale infuocato tra Stella Rossa e Inter Escaldes, ma hanno la meglio i serbi con l'ex Milan Krunic in campo per tutti i 90 minuti nel 2-0 con due espulsioni (una per parte). Pareggi a reti bianche tra Aarhus-Braga e KuPS-Gent, mentre gli elvetici del Thun hanno calato il tris sugli scozzesi degli Hearts, strappando anche un clean sheet.

È bastato infine un solo acuto nel primo tempo al Friburgo di Vincenzo Grifo per superare 1-0 il Trabzonspor guidato dell'ex Roma e Liverpool Salah, mentre il Brighton si conferma in Europa dopo il successo sul Manchester City, espugnando il campo del Getafe per 1-0 grazie al guizzo decisivo arrivato poco dopo l'ora di gioco.

Il Copenaghen ha piegato 2-1 l'Iberia, il Lugano capolista si è sbarazzato dello Žalgiris con un rotondo 3-0 e il Monaco ha sconfitto 2-0 i danesi del Nordsjaelland. Successi casalinghi anche per il Panathinaikos, 2-1 sul CSKA Sofia anche grazie al centro realizzato dall'ex Milan Calabria. Per il Twente gioco da ragazzi il 3-1 in rimonta ai danni del Pafos, danneggiato dall'espulsione di Lele al 64' che ha lasciato in 10 contro 11 i ciprioti. I rumeni dell'Universitatea Craiova hanno regolato l'Egnatia per 2-0, terminano in parità Riga-Jablonec e St. Truiden-Brann.

#2289. Sheffield United man to attract transfer ‘interest’ in January window, says reporter

Sheffield United could face a battle to keep hold of the England youth international in the upcoming January transfer window amid potential attention from other clubs. He is under contract at SUFC until June 2028 meaning he still has just under two years left to run down on his deal at Bramall Lane.

Peck, 22, has become a key player for the Blades in the Championship under the guidance of head coach Chris Wilder. He has made 16 appearances for the South Yorkshire outfit in all competitions this season, 14 of which have come in the league, and he has chipped in with four goals and three assists.

Oxley has shared this update on his situation, as per a report by BBC Sport: “Peck’s stock is high, and rising. He has become a regular in the England under-21 side, he’s one of the first names on the Blades team sheet, and his underlying shooting, passing, possession and defending statistics show he ranks as one of the Championship’s best players in his position.

“He was coveted by Premier League clubs last summer, and you’d imagine he will be the subject of interest once again in January, especially after United sold a trio of stars pre-season to help balance the books.”

Sheffield United won’t want to lose Peck anytime soon, especially halfway through this campaign. He is a valuable member of SUFC’s squad and has the capacity to grow and develop even further down the line.

West Ham were said to be keen on him in the summer after their relegation from the Premier League. However, nothing materialised in the end and he stayed put beyond the last deadline in September.

Peck, who is from Worthing, has enjoyed plenty of game time with the Blades over recent times. He battles it out with the likes of Kalvin Phillips, Oli Arblaster and Joe Rothwell, among others, for minutes in Wilder’s starting XI.

He joined Sheffield United as a youngster back in 2021 after rising up through the academy at Arsenal. He has since played over 100 matches and was also loaned out to Oldham Athletic back in 2022 to get some more experience under his belt down in League Two.

Sheffield United’s chances of retaining the services of Peck in the long run will likely depend on whether they can reach the top flight. If they go up this term, he would probably stick around at SUFC.

If they stay in the second tier though, it would be a surprise if he stayed beyond next year. The Blades need to take advantage of his ability whilst they can.

Wilder’s men have been in good form recently and are genuine contenders for the play-offs if they can stay consistent. They beat Preston North End 3-2 last time out on Tuesday night with Peck scoring a hat-trick at Deepdale against the Lilywhites.

Sheffield United are now unbeaten in their last four and they are starting to build a bit of momentum now as they aim to get into the top eight. They are sat in 9th position in the table and they are only a point behind West Ham in 8th ahead of their upcoming match against Charlton Athletic away.

#2287. Blackburn Rovers vs West Ham predictions: Scott Parker backed for first win in ‘entertaining contest’

Blackburn Rovers head into Saturday’s clash with West Ham sitting 14th in the Championship table. Tony Mowbray’s side have endured an inconsistent start to the campaign, collecting 18 points from 14 games, with five wins, three draws and six defeats leaving them just outside the Championship play-off picture.

Rovers have shown signs of their attacking potential, though, beating Wrexham 2-0 at Ewood Park two weeks ago. Andri Gudjohnsen scored both goals in that victory, taking his league tally to nine and accounting for almost half of Blackburn’s goals this season.

West Ham arrive currently 8th in the Championship with 22 points and have been among the more prolific sides in the league, averaging more than 2.5 goals per game. Scott Parker, appointed following Nuno Espirito Santo’s departure, will be looking for a response after a disappointing result last time out.

WHUFC went three goals down against Cardiff City before eventually rescuing a 3-3 draw. Divine Mukasa, Arne Engels and Max Kilman were all on target in South Wales, but Parker will be concerned by his side’s defensive shortcomings as they prepare for another difficult away assignment.

“Blackburn Rovers have shown enough attacking quality to suggest they can cause West Ham problems, particularly with Gudjohnsen enjoying an excellent run in front of goal. The Icelandic striker has become an important figure for Mowbray, while Todd Cantwell’s creativity gives the hosts another route to hurting their opponents.

“However, West Ham possess considerably more individual quality and should have enough firepower to trouble Rovers’ defence. Jarrod Bowen has been particularly influential, registering seven goals and seven assists in 14 league appearances.

“The visitors will need to improve defensively after their collapse against Cardiff, but their attacking options should ultimately make the difference. Blackburn can contribute to an entertaining contest at Ewood Park, although I expect Parker’s side to come away with all three points.”

“Blackburn Rovers have had some tough games of late. They were narrowly beaten by a great West Brom side, thrashed by Swansea City, and then hard done by to lose to Stoke City after a very soft disallowed goal late on.

“I think Rovers are going to see form come and go this season, largely because their squad isn’t very deep and relies on the form and availability of key figures like Andri Gudjohnsen, Todd Cantwell and Sam Morsy. Despite this, they’re dangerous with their front-footed play under Tony Mowbray and have had some good results at home.

“West Ham will be one to keep an eye on this weekend though. They will have had a couple of days to work under Scott Parker on the training ground after that great comeback draw at Cardiff City.

“We’ll get a better idea of what to expect from WHUFC as they settle into Parker’s management. I do think they have the talent to win the midfield battle though, and with quality players like Jarrod Bowen, I can see them creating the chances to win this one.”

#2285. Panchina Napoli, idea Conceição: la sfida con la Lazio è un dentro o fuori per Allegri

In attesa del dentro o fuori contro la Lazio, la panchina azzurra valuta il profilo di Sergio Conceição come possibile erede.

La pesante sconfitta subita contro il Porto in Champions League e le difficoltà iniziali della stagione hanno fatto scattare i primi dubbi sulla permanenza di Massimiliano Allegri, con indiscrezioni provenienti direttamente dalla Francia precisamente da Foot Mercato, che accostano con insistenza la panchina del Napoli a Sergio Conceição. Questa voce di mercato indica inoltre che la prossima sfida di campionato contro la Lazio rappresenterà un vero e proprio dentro o fuori per il futuro di Allegri.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM

Il profilo del tecnico lusitano non rappresenta una novità per la dirigenza partenopea, che aveva già tentato di ingaggiarlo nel 2021 e nel 2023. In entrambe le occasioni, però, la trattativa era sfumata a causa dell'alta richiesta economica del Porto per la clausola rescissoria. Oggi lo scenario è completamente differente, dato che l'allenatore ha guidato il Milan nella seconda parte della stagione 2024/25 ed è attualmente svincolato, pronto a firmare subito per una nuova squadra.

Forte del recente rifiuto alla proposta avanzata dal Fenerbahçe, l'allenatore attende una chiamata da uno dei cinque principali campionati europei, aprendo concretamente le porte a un ritorno in Serie A. Per il momento si tratta unicamente di una candidatura e non di una trattativa in corso, con il futuro di questa pista che dipenderà strettamente dalle prossime prove della squadra e dal test quasi decisivo di domenica contro la Lazio.

#2284. Tottenham new boys score in shoot-out win over Sydney FC

Tottenham Hotspur fans enjoyed their first glimpse of summer signings Andy Robertson and Sandro Tonali in the shirt, with both players scoring penalties in the shoot-out that followed a 1-1 draw with Sydney FC.

Spurs took the lead through a first-half Mathys Tel free-kick, before Roberto De Zerbi’s youthful defence was undone by Takahiro Sekine, who tucked away one of the Australian side’s only chances of the game.

Magic from Mathys Tel 🪄A brilliant free kick from the Frenchman gets @spursofficial off to a flyer, as the striker puts it top bins to take a 1-0 lead in SydneyWatch #TOTvSYD live and exclusive on Paramount+ 📺 pic.twitter.com/ntqTgleasJ

Tonali was brought on as a half-time substitute, before Robertson took the captain’s armband from Archie Gray after he was introduced in the 65th minute.

The former Liverpool left-back delivered three dangerous crosses which went unconverted, something of a theme for a Spurs team who failed to make the most of long spells of dominance.

James Maddison and Mateus Fernandes were not in the match-day squad, while Pedro Porro, Marcos Senesi, Cristian Romero, Micky van de Ven and Jean Paul van Hecke have yet to join the group after the World Cup.

There was another impressive showing from 17-year-old prospect Luca Williams-Barnett, who is pushing for first-team opportunities this upcoming season.

Penalties followed the final whistle, with Spurs scoring all four of their spot kicks. Goalkeeper Martin Dubravka, signed on a free transfer this summer, saved one and Sydney FC’s Josh Lacey hit the post to give Spurs the spoils 4-2.

Spurs win the shoot-out 4-2. That will be that.

Hoefsloot dives to his right and pushes Donley’s penalty around the post.

But then Dubravka saves from Popovic, and Spurs remain 3-2 up. Score the next one and they win the shoot-out.

Very similar placing to Tonali’s penalty. Does Dubravka have a save in him?

He doesn’t need to have one because Josh Lacey has hit the post. 3-2 to Spurs after three pens each.

Plenty of power and right into the side netting. No mistake from Spurs’s big money summer signing.

Dubravka then guesses the right way, but Toure finds the bottom left corner. 2-2.

The 17-year-old takes the mickey a little bit, dinking the ball straight down the middle. Spurs score their first penalty.

Then Popovic steps up and sends Dubravka the wrong way. 1-1.

Spurs were the game’s dominant force, but they did not convert that control into enough goals. No cause for alarm though, and no injuries from what we can tell. There will be some penalties on the way.

Williams-Barnett with a superb piece of control and turn forward, but the danger was snuffed out as he dribbled the ball into the penalty area. Then the youngster shoots from outside the box, deflected behind for a corner.

Andy Robertson has been impressive, and the goalkeeper makes a fingertip save to flick his low cross away from danger. Almost third time lucky for Yang who was waiting at the back post for a tap-in.

Andy Robertson's first outing as a Spurs player 🫡 pic.twitter.com/q5bdzQknJ2

Spurs controlling possession, pushing for the goal that would spare them having to take some penalties. As happens with this friendlies, the game has become more bitty since all the changes.

If the game finishes as a draw, there will be a penalty shoot-out. Donley has fizzed some crisp forward passes since coming on in midfield. Then Donley underlaps, picked out by Williams-Barnett but his low cross is straight at the goalkeeper.

Andy Robertson getting forward to good effect once again, standing up a cross for Yang in the middle but the substitute heads wide from seven or eight yards out.

Referee waves play on as Spurs pour forward and Robertson flashes a ball across the box, and the slight deflection was enough to put off Yang at the back post and he missed the target. Should have been a tap in.

Spurs close to a second, but Tonali’s shot from the edge of the box is pushed around the post. There was more good approach play from Williams-Barnett to tee up the Italian.

More Spurs changes: Andy Robertson is on, and takes the armband, he replaces Kyerematen. Up front, Richarlison and Solomon are off, replaced by Min-Hyeok and Dane Scarlett. Donley and Melia replace Gray and Gallagher in midfield.

A couple of appeals for a Spurs penalty after Kyerematen burst beyond the Sydney defence from left-back. He could have crossed sooner, but was tackled, and then there was a challenge on Richarlison. Referee waves it away.

Very youthful Spurs back four on the pitch now, which played a part in the nature of the equaliser they conceded. No Romero, Van de Ven, Van Hecke or Senesi available for selection today, but Andy Robertson is warming up on the touchline.

Spurs straight back into another long spell of possession, with Tonali winning a foul in midfield after a smooth turn forward.

A touch of ill fortunate for Spurs, the half-time substitute Takai inadvertently poked the ball through to Sekine who lifted the ball over Dubravka to equalise. Delicate finish, and Spurs are breached.

Conor Gallagher still closing down tirelessly, but he has been a little untidy with the ball at his feet. I suspect he was the bleep test winner in training. Sydney do well to play through the pressure and keep possession for a while.

Good industry from Tonali in midfield to regain possession, and Williams-Barnett shows real poise on the ball again. Easy to see why Spurs are excited about him.

Kyerematen defends well at the back post when it looked like Macallister was about to head at goal.

Then Spurs are away on the break, and Williams-Barnett skims the crossbar with a left-footed shot from a tight angle.

Three half-time Spurs changes: Tel, Bergvall and Davies off, Takai, Tonali and Williams-Barnett are on. Takai goes to centre-back with 17-year-old Williams-Barnett in an attacking midfield position.

A decent half’s work from Spurs, they look in a good place physically and their high pressing has caught the eye. Not quite clinical enough in the penalty area so far though, they have butchered some good chances.

Sydney have come to life as an attacking force, Spurs’s defence undone by a ball over the top. Dubravka caught in no-man’s-land, and Mac Allister poked the ball beyond him but did not generate enough power to score.

Cracking effort from the Sydney forward Macallister, trying to chip Dubravka from some 45 yards out. The goalkeeper was worried and scrambling, the effort misses the target.

Sydney looking ragged now, and Gallagher cracks a shot off the foot of the post from the edge of the box. Then Youlley takes on a shot from long range which is high, wide and handsome. Richarlison is then fouled by Popovic, dragging down the forward to stop a counter. Yellow card.

Conor Gallagher is charging forward at every opportunity, applying pressure on Sydney’s defenders whenever they have the ball. With no European football, Spurs can really lean into a high-octane approach this season.

Great take, right footed to the the goalkeeper’s side, and the strike was too powerful for Hoefsloot. A clean hit, and Spurs now lead. A well-deserved goal on the balance of play.

The game has slipped into a lull now, after a bright Spurs start. De Zerbi’s team do now have a free-kick at the edge of the D after Manor Solomon is fouled.

Tel amnd Gallagher threaten down the left for Spurs, with the midfielder finding the winger with a reverse pass. Tel’s cross is cleared.

Then Sydney muster their first shot of the game, Youlley with a strike from 25 yards out which Dubravka pushes away from danger.

Sydney FC starting to get their foot on the ball a little more now, but still no sign that they have capability to hurts Spurs going forward. Kyerematen is then fouled in the Sydney half.

Sydney are yet to have a touch in the Spurs penalty area, it has been one-way traffic so far. De Zerbi will be pleased with what he has watched so far, but no killer touch in the box as yet.

Conor Gallagher with a nice touch to win a free-kick near the left touchline. Sydney just about hanging on. The goalkeeper claims Tel’s cross from the free-kick.

Spurs’s closing down is choking Sydney’s build up play, and Gallagher wastes a good chance when free in the box. Shot blocked when there was time and space to pick his spot.

Lucas Bervall’s low cross is turned behind for a corner and Spurs remain in the ascendancy. Another threatening delivery, and Ben Davies may well have had a shout for a penalty, dragged to the turf by Grant. If this was a Premier League game, I’m sure VAR would have taken a close look at that.

Hoefsloot with a really poor pass from his six-yard box, straight into the path of Tel 25 yards out, but his side-footed effort was saved by the goalkeeper. Pitches like this make technical errors an inevitability.

Sydney’s goalkeeper Hoefsloot punches a corner clear under some pressure, attacking set-pieces were a rare positive for Spurs last season. The Premier League team are dominating possession in the early minutes.

Conor Gallagher and Richarlison leading an aggressive Tottenham press in the early exchanges. Tel enjoys plenty of touches down the left flank, but his inswinging cross from the left is headed clear. Rio Kyerematen is puhsing on from left-back.

After a rendition of Oh When The Saints Go Marching In on the trumpet, we are under way. A chance for Aussie Spurs fans to feel like they are in N17 for the evening.

The pitch looks slightly more lush than the surface Chelsea had to play on across town yesterday. The Allianz Stadium looks distinctly similar to the Etihad. Archie Gray captains Spurs.

No James Maddison in the squad for this game, perhaps still being managed physically after last year’s serious knee injury. Suspect we will see a more senior side picked for the friendly against Chelsea on Saturday.

The 21-year-old has a sweet left foot, on display when he scored this goal against Manchester City while on loan at Leyton Orient.

JAMIE DONLEY. THAT'S INCREDIBLE. 🤯The @SpursOfficial loanee with an incredible effort from distance that ends up in the net to give @leytonorientfc the opening goal against Manchester City 😱#EmiratesFACup pic.twitter.com/bHnKg92Q2y

Lucas Bergvall has been linked with a move away from Spurs, but he starts in midfield. No Fernandes in the squad at all. No summer signings in the starting line-up, but Tonali and Andy Robertson are on the bench.

Spurs starting XI: Dubravka; Kyerematen, Davies, Hardy, Tye Hall; Gray, Bergvall, Solomon, Gallagher, Tel; Richarlison

Subs: Kinsky, Robertson, Takai, Tingey, Byrne, Tyrese Hall, Russell-Denny, Donley, Tonali, Ajayi, Yang, Williams-Barnett, Scarlett

Spurs fans took their first look at summer signing Mateus Fernandes in a 2-0 victory over Auckland, and their pre-season tour continues today against Sydney FC.

Fernandes, an £85m purchase from West Ham United, also scored a stunning volley in a behind-closed-doors game against MK Dons.

Sandro Tonali is part of the travelling squad for these friendlies, as is new centre-back Jean Paul van Hecke. Marcos Senesi, Cristian Romero and Pedro Porro have been given extra time off after their respective nations reached the World Cup final, won by Porro and Spain.

Van Hecke and Senesi ranked very highly among defenders for progressive passing, which offers an insight into the qualities Roberto De Zerbi is prioritising this summer.

The Italian likes his teams to bait opponents into pressing them high up the pitch, before moving the ball through central areas using third-man combinations and wall passes. The addition of two ball-playing centre-backs and two new central midfielders should mean Spurs can play like a recognisable De Zerbi team.

While Dane Scarlett and Richarlison scored against Auckland, Spurs’s squad still lacks high-class options in forward areas, with a move for Bournemouth’s Eli Junior Kroupi mooted earlier in the summer.

Spurs fans will be excited to watch 17-year-old Luca Williams-Barnett, the midfielder who is one of the outstanding players in his age group in the country.

“He’s a talent,” Ledley King said. “There’s a lot of hard work ahead of him, but there’s no doubt that he’s someone with great ability.

“He’s seen players like Harry Kane come through the academy and, through sheer hard work and determination, put themselves in a position to kick on. He couldn’t have a better role model.

“There’s no doubt we’re excited by his talent and the next part will be up to him.”

#2283. Calciomercato no stop - Indiscrezioni, trattative e retroscena del 5 novembre

INTER, LO SCHIAVO NUOVO DIRECTOR OF FOOTBALL DEVELOPMENT. ROMA, NEL MIRINO UN ESTERNO: PIACCIONO GITTENS E KVERNADZE. IL MILAN PAGHERÀ 3,5 MILIONI DI EURO PER AVERE KROSCHE. JUVENTUS, PER IL FUTURO OCCHI SU KOVACS. NAPOLI, MCTOMINAY CHIEDE TROPPO: RINNOVO DIFFICILE. IL TORINO SEGUE MIKOLAJEWSKI DEL PARMA.

La notizia era già nell'aria, ma adesso è arrivata anche l'ufficialità: Simone Lo Schiavo è il nuovo Director of Football Development dell'Inter. A renderlo noto è lo stesso club nerazzurro attraverso un comunicato sul proprio sito, nel quale lo ha accolto.

Il mercato di gennaio sarà fondamentale per la Roma. La priorità individuata dalla dirigenza è acquistare un esterno offensivo in grado di garantire imprevedibilità. Tra i nomi seguiti figurano Jamie Gittens del Chelsea, Endrick del Real Madrid, Jamie Leweling dello Stoccarda e Giorgi Kvernadze del Frosinone. In particolare, scrive oggi La Gazzetta dello Sport, quello del talento in forza ai Blues è un pro­filo che piace e che era stato già inse­guito nella sessione estiva.

Il Milan è pronto a pagare la clausola di risoluzione automatica per permettere a Markus Krosche di lasciare l'Eintracht Francoforte e diventare l'Head of Football dei rossoneri. Il Diavolo verserà nelle casse dei tedeschi 3,5 milioni di euro, il dirigente sarà operativo dall'1 gennaio 2027.

La Juventus ha sfidato l'AZ di Bendeguz Kovacs, attaccante del club olandese che i torinesi seguono con attenzione. Già la scorsa estate i bianconeri avevano provato a prenderlo a zero, ma il rinnovo fino al 2029 ha frenato la trattativa. A riportarlo è Tuttosport.

Scott McTominay chiedeva al Napoli 12 milioni di euro all'anno per rinnovare, poi però con il passare del tempo il centrocampista ha abbassato le proprie pretese, arrivando fino a 10. L'impressione è che a 8-9 si potrebbe chiudere l'accordo per il rinnovo, ma difficilmente De Laurentiis accetterà certe cifre e di conseguenza in estate la cessione resta un'ipotesi.

Il Torino continua a seguire l’attaccante polacco Daniel Mikolajewski, classe 2006 che sta facendo molto bene con la maglia del Lucerna, ma di proprietà del Parma. La valutazione in questi mesi è aumentata in maniera considerevole, si parla infatti non a caso di una cifra tra gli 8 e i 10 milioni di euro.

KANE RINNOVA COL BAYERN, RAPHINHA CON IL BARCELLONA. ALISSON VERSO L’ADDIO AL LIVERPOOL: CI SONO DUE CLUB BRASILIANO. EMERY-ASTON VILLA, PRONTO IL RINNOVO

Due rinnovi importanti per due top club europei: il Bayern Monaco ha infatti annunciato il rinnovo di Harry Kane che ha firmato fino al 30 giugno 2029. Il Pallone d’Oro 2026 ha scelto di proseguire la sua avventura in Baviera, dove dal suo arrivo nell’estate 2023 è diventato il simbolo del nuovo corso del club tedesco. Il Barcellona blinda uno dei protagonisti della sua nuova era. Il club catalano ha annunciato il rinnovo di contratto di Raphael Dias Belloli, meglio conosciuto come Raphinha, che ha prolungato il proprio accordo fino al 30 giugno 2030. Una scelta che certifica il peso raggiunto dal brasiliano all'interno del progetto blaugrana, dopo un percorso iniziato nell'estate del 2022.

Il futuro di Alisson Becker sarà lontano dal Liverpool con cui andrà a scadenza di contratto al termine della stagione. Sul portiere brasiliano potrebbe esserci nuovamente l’interesse della Juventus, che l’aveva seguito in estate, anche se al momento il Brasile sembra essere un’opzione più concreta. Il giocatore piace infatti molto al Flamengo, nonostante l’età non più giovanissima del portiere e l’ingaggio elevato, e all’Internacional Porto Alegre, club nel quale Alisson è cresciuto e a cui è rimasto fortemente legato, avendo in passato già espresso il desiderio di farvi ritorno.

Unai Emery è vicino a blindare il suo futuro all'Aston Villa e a spegnere definitivamente le voci su un possibile interesse del Manchester United. Il tecnico spagnolo, protagonista della rinascita del club negli ultimi quattro anni, è pronto a firmare un nuovo accordo (quello attuale scade nel 2029) con i Villans dopo i colloqui avanzati avuti mercoledì con il presidente Nassef Sawiris.

#2282. ‘Catalyst’ victory can inspire Wrexham to a result in Wolves clash: Predictions

Wrexham beat league leaders Middlesbrough at home on Wednesday night. George Thomason and Ollie Rathbone scored two late goals for the Welsh outfit as they returned to winning ways in impressive fashion.

The Red Dragons are sat in 16th place in the Championship table after their first 14 fixtures and they have made a slow start to the season. They are only six points off the play-offs now behind West Ham in 8th position.

As for Wolves, they came from behind away at Bristol City last time out to win 2-1. Newcastle United loan man Sean Neave scored two second-half goals to earn WWFC an important three points at Ashton Gate against the Robins.

Cesar Peixoto‘s men have now risen into 2nd in the division behind Middlesbrough ahead of Birmingham City. The Midlands club were relegated from the Premier League earlier this year after they finished in the bottom three along with West Ham and Burnley.

“Wrexham’s win over Middlesbrough was much needed and has eased some pressure off Phil Parkinson. It has been a tough season for the Red Dragons so far and they will be eager to hit some form now.

“The Welsh side haven’t scored enough goals in this campaign and are lacking a cutting edge. In fact, only six teams have scored less than them in the Championship so far.

“Wolves found a way to win at Bristol City which is a good sign for a team eyeing automatic promotion. WWFC are now unbeaten in their last five games since their home defeat to Bolton Wanderers last month.

“Cesar Peixoto’s squad is littered with Premier League quality and they will fancy their chances in North Wales. However, I think it may end a high scoring draw with the hosts seemingly back on track now.”

“Wrexham produced arguably their best performance of the season to beat Middlesbrough on Wednesday night. That has to be a catalyst for Phil Parkinson if he’s to hold onto his job and if the Red Dragons are to push up the Championship table.

“Another tricky game awaits here with Wolves unbeaten in five, but another home match marks a chance for the North Welsh side to build some momentum and head into the break on a high.

“Wolves are in high spirits themselves though. They’ve responded to poor form with a five-game unbeaten run, the most recent being an impressive comeback win thanks to a Sean Neave brace. That will be a real confidence boost for the young striker as well, as he looks to step up to the senior game and deliver while Wanderers star Raul Jimenez is out.

“This is a tough one to call, as Wrexham are capable of picking up another win if they play like they did on Wednesday. However, I can’t see Wolves losing, so I’ll say this ends level.”

#2279. L'incredibile controsenso post derby di Milan e Inter. Amorim e la doppia faccia insospettabile: bene in Serie A, disastro in Europa. La terza risposta della Juve su Spalletti: Rennes, Napoli e AZ, la squadra è con lui. Anche grazie a Carnevali

Il disastro del Milan, quello sfiorato dall'Atalanta e l'ennesimo sorriso europeo della Juventus. Questo, in estrema sintesi, il bilancio del giovedì di coppe per le italiane: due allenatori su tre non possono certo sorridere, Amorim e Sarri, mentre Spalletti, pur con troppa sofferenza nel finale, può farlo eccome, ma ci torneremo più avanti. Per prima cosa, infatti, il tema che vogliamo affrontare, tornando anche indietro di due giorni, è quello che riguarda l'incredibile e senza senso ritorno in campo di Inter e Milan dopo il derby di sabato scorso. A San Siro avevamo assistito a una partita che ci aveva lasciato un messaggio chiaro e preciso: rossoneri in netta crescita e nerazzurri sulle gambe dopo le tante gare giocate partendo da situazione di svantaggio che avevano lasciato il segno. Il calcio, però, e lo sappiamo molto bene, è strano, stranissimo. Tutto può cambiare in un attimo e spesso non accade ciò che sembra essere quasi scontato. Detto fatto. L'Inter di Chivu ha spazzato via il Feyenoord in trasferta, andando a mille all'ora e ripartendo dopo la prima batosta presa in campionato, con tanto di ennesimo derby perso, mentre il Milan si è consegnato al Ferencvaros a San Siro, uscendo tra i fischi di uno stadio che soltanto cinque giorni prima aveva dato vita a una vera e propria festa.

Un controsenso, appunto, perché il derby, almeno sulla carta, dovrebbe dare una spinta clamorosa a chi lo vince e mettere dubbi in testa a chi, invece, esce sconfitto, la le gare di Inter prima e Milan poi in Europa ci hanno detto l'esatto opposto. Poi un altro aspetto, incredibile anche questo. Ruben Amorim, tecnico portoghese arrivato in Serie A l'estate scorsa, sulla panchina rossonera, sta facendo un percorso completamente diverso tra campionato ed Europa League. Fin qui, in un certo senso, sarebbe anche una cosa che ci potevamo aspettare, però al contrario. Spieghiamoci meglio: un allenatore, spesso, nei primi mesi in Italia, arrivando dall'estero, può andare incontro ad alcuni problemi, prevedibili, viste le particolari caratteristiche del nostro calcio, per trovarsi più a suo agio nelle competizioni internazionali, ma ad Amorim sta succedendo l'opposto. Bene in Serie A, visti i 21 punti raccolti nelle prime dieci giornate, solo quattro in meno dell'Inter campione d'Italia, e male in Europa League, dove di fatto ha già compromesso, con la sua squadra, ma qualificazione diretta agli ottavi di finale, avendo solo tre punti dopo le prime quattro gare. Strano, molto strano.

Infine un capitolo a parte sulla Juventus, dopo la terza vittoria in Europa. L'ultimo periodo è stato complicatissimo, lo sappiamo e lo abbiamo detto in tutte le salse, ma ci sono state tre partite delle ultime quattro che ci hanno detto una cosa inequivocabile: lo spogliatoio è con Luciano Spalletti. I tre indizi che fanno una prova sono le gare contro Rennes, Napoli e AZ, lasciando da parte quelle contro Lecce e Genoa. Nel momento di massima pressione i giocatori hanno lottato con il coltello tra i denti, dimostrando di essere dalla parte del tecnico e adesso il vento sembra davvero essere cambiato. Le parole di Giovanni Carnevali dopo il ko a Marassi hanno fatto il resto. Il dirigente ha parlato alla squadra, ha confermato l'allenatore e ha alzato i toni chiedendo responsabilità a chi va in campo gara dopo gara. Un discorso duro, che ha pagato e sta pagando. Adesso la Juve sfiderà la Fiorentina, poi ci sarà la sosta. Con tre punti al Franchi la crisi sarebbe solo un lontano ricordo. Sia chiaro.
